sentence: This project builds a rapid test, using transcriptomic technology, to show which drugs work against Mycobacterium abscessus, a drug-resistant pathogen that causes lung infections.
This project develops a CRISPR repair method that uses patient-derived stem cells to make retinal cells for transplant back into the same patient.
This project studies which genes drive the shift from moderate to excessive alcohol drinking, using a single cell approach to find molecular mechanisms.
This project tries to solve problems in treating head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, such as toxicities and low immunotherapy response rates.
This project builds tools that bring together, share and show data on genes and cells linked to human pain.
This project studies how a dentate spike, a hippocampal event, becomes epileptiform activity in mouse models of Alzheimer’s disease, and whether neuromodulation restores circuit function.
This project gathers and links clinical, imaging and biological data on rectal cancer, uses machine learning to find immune phenotypes, and shares the data.
This project tests whether mechanical forces directly drive how tissue is assembled in the corneal stromal matrix made by human corneal cells.
This project builds a model that combines imaging and non-imaging biomarkers to predict the risk of Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma using deep learning.
This project uses AI modeling to find how alcohol changes the causes and pathways leading to death in patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome.
This project develops selective inhibitors of an enzyme called neuronal nitric oxide synthase to treat melanoma.
This project studies how little cigars and cigarillos fit into the use of multiple tobacco products and cannabis in young adults.
This project studies how a loss of inhibitory control damages neurons in neuroHIV with opioid use disorder, using cultured murine and human cells.
This project studies which microbial and environmental factors drive chronic dermatophyte infection in an endemic population, using data on microbiome composition and fungal genetics.
This project tests whether genetically enhanced donor hepatocytes can expand in vivo to treat liver diseases and avoid immune responses without immune suppression.
This project studies the earliest stages of the HIV reservoir in naïve T cells, using a barcoded virus ex vivo.
This project studies how cancer patients and murine models respond to immune checkpoint inhibitors to find the immune cells that kill tumor cells.
This project builds models that use suicide risk assessments and electronic health records to predict suicide risk and guide outpatient treatment.
This project studies unintended consequences and ethical issues that may come from screening and intervention for toddler mental health.
This project builds personalized models of aggression using data from surveys and sensors on smartphones and wearable devices in daily life.
